source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Digital Twin aerial LiDAR point cloud, 23-ku (2023) + OpenStreetMap
license: CC BY 4.0 (point cloud, Tokyo Metropolitan Government) + ODbL (OpenStreetMap footprints/roads)
attribution: 東京都デジタルツイン実現プロジェクト 区部点群データ (Tokyo Metropolitan Government, CC BY 4.0); © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
method: aerial LiDAR ~48 pts/m2 binned at 1 m; ground = LAS class 2 median DEM; buildings = OSM footprints filled to cloud roof height; vegetation = non-last returns / green RGB; no poles (not resolvable in aerial LiDAR); roads/sidewalks from OSM highway buffers
notes: Terrain is solid below the surface (class 1). Aerial LiDAR cannot resolve poles (only wires show as horizontal lines) and cannot see walls or tree trunks; trunks are synthesised below canopies. Anything above the 100 m box is clipped. voxel z grows southward.
